missions.name: Break of Dawn
missions.summary: This place is not safe. Maybe you can find some help in the nearby house.
missions.description:
Upon arrival back at Iboholmen after your group's weekend excursion on an island, it becomes immediately clear that something is not right. Something destroyed your boat, with you barely making it onto shore alive. You are injured and defenseless.

Whatever it was, the thing that attacked your boat seems to have moved on, but the place seems eerily abandoned. Maybe there are people hiding in the nearby house that can tell you a bit more about what is going on.

You are now armed and can defend yourself. However, it would be good to have a safe location to hold up in and return to should things turn for the worst.

In the house at Yttervik, you heard a terrified young woman named Therese tried in vain to get in touch with her grandparents and was in dire need of help.

Following the road should lead you to Iboholmen Church where Therese said she took refuge. If you are not too late, she may be able to help you understand what happened in the last few days.

missions.name: Civil Defense
missions.summary: Investigate the town to find any information on the evacuation.
missions.description:
Therese's hopes have been crushed: despite evidence that the population was brought there, even the bomb shelter at Salthamn is empty, and the town is empty. Her grandparents, her friend Anita, all their neighbors - the whole population has all but vanished, and whoever was left behind has been ruthlessly killed.

Both you and Therese have now guessed that the situation is even bleaker than you could possibly imagine. All you can do now is explore the bomb shelter and the town: it's your best chance of finding any answers about this mass disappearance and about the machines, and the last glimmer of hope for Therese.

One of the handful of people that did not die in the bombing of the Måsskär camp, Jenny, used to volunteer for supply runs. She and her twin sister Anna, both retired professional racing cyclists, would race against each other, as a way to have some fun despite the tragic circumstances.

Two days before Måsskär fell, Jenny's sister left to drop off some supplies in a container, for any other group of survivors to find and take, but never returned. Her destination was Åsötungan, the narrow patch of land connecting the Archipelago region to the rest of Östertörn. Jenny asked you to look for her, and challenged you to take part in their competition.

Before finding refuge in the tunnels of the Ringfort to escape a swarm of machines, Veronika hid for a few days in a cellar at Ängsäs Manor, on the west coast in the Sävered Region, together with an Air Force Vråken fighter pilot called Elsa Khorsandi. Soon afterwards, they got separated and never saw each other again; but thanks to you, Veronika was delighted to find out that Elsa is still alive and safe in Hotel Björntunet on the island of Himfjäll. Maybe Elsa left a clue for Veronika in that cellar?

Veronika explained how FNIX's Ticks were busy putting up walls and connecting a lot of mysterious electrical devices. She suspects those might be supercomputers based on the Gray models they had at FOA 53; maybe FNIX is setting up data centers of sorts to increase its computational and storage capacity? In any case, destroying them would be a "thorn in FNIX's side", to use her words.

She warned you that there are a lot of machines guarding the location, so FNIX is clearly deeming this a key structure to protect. So this time around, maybe she recommended you use stealth to infiltrate the facility, rather than engage the machines head-on.

The Army dispatched a reconnaissance squad, which reported they had managed to track an enemy emitter shortly before they lost contact.

Klas's memories from inside the machine network led you to the Norrmyra Artillery Range where you discovered a destroyed rocket launch silo.
